# The Nicene case, supplemented


Ken Kibbey's *Living Systematic Theology* (LST) confesses the Son and the Spirit
God, and the three persons, from a few texts read in its own way. The last two
chapters found that the weighing cannot choose between that reading and the
readings of its two rivals: Jehovah's Witnesses, for whom the Son is "a god" and
a creature, and the Oneness Pentecostal David Bernard, for whom Father, Son and
Spirit are one person. This chapter asks what the older defenders of the
confession, and some newer ones, add. The case it builds goes beyond what LST
argues. The library assembles it from cited sources, every one of its readings
old, and marks its results as proposed (⚗), so that a reader can tell what the
library constructs from what it reports.

## More routes to "the Son is God"

LST rests the Son's deity on John 1:1 and 1:3, with Thomas's words in John 20:28
among its texts. Christians have read 20:28 as a route of its own, and four more
texts the same way, and the Witnesses have answered each:

- Thomas's "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:28). Augustine: Thomas "saw and
  touched the man, and acknowledged the God whom he neither saw nor touched".
  The Witnesses: "To Thomas, Jesus was like 'a god'".
- "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever" (Hebrews 1:8). Calvin: whoever reads
  the verse "cannot doubt but that the Messiah is called God". The New World
  Translation, the Witnesses' Bible: "God is your throne", because verse 9, "God,
  your God, anointed you", shows the one addressed is "one of his worshippers".
- "Our great God and Savior Jesus Christ" (Titus 2:13). Granville Sharp (1798;
  cited here from the edition of 1803) argued that when the Greek word for "the"
  stands once before two nouns joined by "and", as it does before "God" and
  "Savior", one person is meant, so that Christ is "not only entitled God, but
  even the 'great God'". The New World Translation reads two persons: "the great
  God and of our Savior, Jesus Christ".
- "The Christ, who is God over all, blessed forever" (Romans 9:5). Calvin: "the
  words most evidently mean this". The New World Translation puts a full stop
  before "God" and reads a praise of the Father.
- "At the name of Jesus every knee should bow" (Philippians 2:10–11), which is
  what Isaiah 45:23 says of the LORD. Calvin: "everything may be accomplished in
  him that God, by the prophet Isaiah, exclusively claims to himself". The
  Witnesses read the honour as given "to the glory of God the Father", by one
  greater.

With LST's route from John 1:1 these are six routes to one conclusion, and the
library proves what an opponent must reject to overturn it: the reading of each
of the six, and nothing less (`son_is_god_burden`).

## The Fathers against the modalists and the Arians

A modalist holds the Father, the Son and the Spirit to be one person showing
himself in three ways, as Oneness does. Tertullian wrote *Against Praxeas* about
213 against one, Praxeas, who, he says, "put to flight the Paraclete [the
Helper, the Holy Spirit], and … crucified the Father". Two of his arguments answer
the Oneness reading directly. When Jesus says the law asks for two witnesses and
names himself and the Father (John 8:17–18), "if He were one — being at once both
the Son and the Father — He certainly would not have quoted the sanction of the
law, which requires not the testimony of one, but of two". And when the Son asks
on earth and the Father answers from heaven (John 12:28; Matthew 17:5), "how many
Persons do you discover, obstinate Praxeas? Are there not as many as there are
voices?" Bernard answers both: the two witnesses, he says, are "the Father (the
divine Spirit) and the man Jesus", and the voice is "only another manifestation of
the omnipresent Spirit of God". Tertullian's own account comes close to the
Oneness reading at one point: before creation, he says, the Word was God's "own
Thought", what "the Greeks call λόγος" (*logos*, "word" or "reason") (ch. 5),
and only at creation a second person (ch. 7). That concession is not encoded.

Arius, the Alexandrian priest who held the Son a creature, read "firstborn of all
creation" (Colossians 1:15) much as the Witnesses do. Athanasius, writing against
the Arians, answers that all things were created in the Son, so "He is other than
the creatures, and is not a creature, but the Creator of the creatures". Arius
had already granted that the Son is over the rest of creation and still called
him a creature, "a perfect creature of God, but not as one of the creatures", so
the step is rated `disputed`, the lowest of the library's four ratings, given
when a cited reader grants a step's starting points and denies its conclusion.

Bruce Metzger (1953) answers "a god" from the one God of Scripture: "if the
Jehovah's Witnesses take this translation seriously, they are polytheists". The
Witnesses reply from John 10:34, where Jesus quotes "you are gods": "Since these
are referred to as 'gods,' mighty ones, surely Jesus can be and is 'a god'". And
some Christian readers grant Metzger's premise and still hold the Word God:
Origen calls him "a second God", and Justin "another God and Lord subject to the
Maker of all things". So Metzger's step is rated `disputed` too.

## What "is God" means

Both rivals reason from one reading of the words "is God": that to call someone
God, in the full sense, is to say he is the one God himself, so that two who are
God are the same. (The Witnesses allow a lesser sense, "a god", as their reply to
Metzger shows.) Bernard concludes that Jesus, being God, is "the Father manifested
in flesh". The Witnesses' brochure reasons the other way, that one who is "with"
God "cannot be the same as" God, and so is not God. Basil gave another reading in
the fourth century: "ousia [essence] has the same relation to hypostasis [person]
as the common has to the particular". "God" names the one essence the Father, the
Son and the Spirit share, and "Father", "Son" and "Spirit" name the persons. The
creed of the Council of Nicaea (325) had already confessed the Son "of one
substance (ὁμοούσιον) with the Father".

The library checks a smaller thing than either reading: what Bernard's step does
to three claims a reader may think collide, that the Father is God, the Son is
God, and the Son is another than the Father. Written as three claims, they can
all be true at once, and they stay so with Basil's reading added, which rules
out reading "is God" as identity (`three_claims_hold_on_one_essence`). Add
Bernard's step, from "each is the one God" to "they are the same person", and
they cannot (`three_claims_fail_on_identity`). The check does not model what
"essence" and "person" mean; that analysis is not yet done.

The step is where Bernard parts, and an orthodox reader denies it. Thomas Aquinas
holds each person the one God himself, since "in God essence is not really
distinct from person", and still holds the Son another than the Father. Things
identical with the same thing are identical with each other, he answers, only
"if the identity be real and logical". Because Aquinas grants Bernard's starting
point and denies his step, the step is rated `disputed`. The same Aquinas rates
Basil's step `disputed` as well: he grants the one essence and still holds each
person the one God himself. So the Nicene case as built here denies something
Aquinas affirms, and he parts from the rivals only at the step to one person.
The disagreement is over what "is God" and "the same" mean, and the Nicene
confession is not shown to contradict itself.

## What the weighing finds

Two positions tie when each defeats the other and the ratings do not choose. A
position is forced when it is accepted however the ties are settled, and it can
be defended when some consistent way of settling them accepts it.

Supplemented, the Nicene case still ties with each rival, and nothing is forced
(`supplemented_forces_nothing`). The Nicene case can be defended
(`nicene_case_defensible`), and so can each rival: the Witnesses on their own
(`witnesses_answering_defensible`), and Oneness together with the six routes
(`nicene_case_not_forced`). Each reading aimed at a rival is answered by that
rival with a cited reading of its own, rated the same: Bernard on the witnesses
and the voice, the Witnesses on the other "gods". Every reading on both sides is
rated `disputed`. Because the weighing ranks a position by its weakest reading,
six routes weigh there no more than one, and the breadth raises the burden
instead: to deny that the Son is God a reader must reject the reading of each of
six routes, and the Witnesses do, each with a rendering of their own
(`son_is_god_burden`). Oneness also holds that the Son is God, so the six routes
can be defended alongside it (`son_is_god_defensible_with_oneness`). Only the
Witnesses' position defeats them, and it can still be defended
(`son_is_god_not_forced`).

The meanings of these claims are not yet analysed (see the page on how far each
argument is checked). When they are, the fallacy checks can test whether either
side reads "God" in two senses where its step needs one.

### The rivals' replies

<a id="otherGodsAnswerMetzger"></a>
**`otherGodsAnswerMetzger`**

The Witnesses' step: Scripture rightly calls others "gods", so "a god" is not
a second God.

If each of these holds,

<div class="testimony-derivation">

- (1) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-62}{P_{62}}\\) John 10:34–35; Psalm 82:6 — "I said, you are gods" — *consensus*: John 10:34; Ps 82:6
- (2) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-68}{P_{68}}\\) Scripture rightly calls others "gods", so the Word can be "a god" — *disputed*: [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 28; [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1986](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-questions-from-readers-1986), p. 31
- \\(\therefore\\) \\(\lnot \href{claims.html#claim-67}{P_{67}}\\) *denied:* A Word who is "a god" beside the one God would be a second god

</div>

In symbols, the step is \\((\href{claims.html#claim-62}{P_{62}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-68}{P_{68}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-67}{P_{67}}\\).

**The Witnesses' reply from John 10:34**: "Since these are referred to as
'gods,' mighty ones, surely Jesus can be and is 'a god.'"

<div class="testimony-derivation">

- (1) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-62}{P_{62}}\\) — John 10:34–35; Psalm 82:6 — "I said, you are gods"
- (2) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-68}{P_{68}}\\) — Scripture rightly calls others "gods", so the Word can be "a god"
- (3) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-62}{P_{62}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-68}{P_{68}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-67}{P_{67}}\\)
- \\(\vdash\\) \\(\lnot \href{claims.html#claim-67}{P_{67}}\\) — *at issue, the denial of:* A Word who is "a god" beside the one God would be a second god

- \\(\therefore\\) \\(\lnot \href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\) *denied:* The Word who became flesh in Jesus is God, of God's nature and not created

In symbols, the step is \\((\href{claims.html#claim-71}{P_{71}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-59}{P_{59}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-46}{P_{46}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\).

- (5) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-42}{P_{42}}\\) — In "the Word was God" (John 1:1) the Word has the nature of the one God
- (6) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-43}{P_{43}}\\) — By John 1:3 the Word is not among the things made
- (7) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-37}{P_{37}}\\) — Acts 5:3–4 — "lie to the Holy Spirit … not to man but to God"
- (8) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-44}{P_{44}}\\) — In Acts 5:3–4 Peter names the Holy Spirit God
- (9) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}}\\) — John 1:1 — "the Word was with God"
- (10) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-39}{P_{39}}\\) — John 17:5 — "the glory that I had with you before the world existed"
- (11) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-40}{P_{40}}\\) — Matthew 28:19 — "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit"
- (12) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-51}{P_{51}}\\) — The Word of John 1:1 is God's thought and self-expression, not a second person
- (13) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-52}{P_{52}}\\) — The glory of John 17:5 was the Son's in God's plan before the world
- (14) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-53}{P_{53}}\\) — The one "name" of Matthew 28:19 is Jesus; Father, Son and Spirit are titles
- (15) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-60}{P_{60}}\\) — John 8:17–18 — "the testimony of two people is true … and the Father"
- (16) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-65}{P_{65}}\\) — The two witnesses are the divine Spirit and the man Jesus, of one person
- (17) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-61}{P_{61}}\\) — Matthew 17:5; John 12:28 — the Father answers the Son from heaven
- (18) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-66}{P_{66}}\\) — The voice from heaven is a manifestation of the one Spirit, not a person
- (19) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-71}{P_{71}}\\) — "Is God" says someone is the one God himself, the same one
- (20) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-59}{P_{59}}\\) — 1 Corinthians 8:6 — "for us there is one God, the Father"
- (21) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\) — The Word who became flesh in Jesus is God, of God's nature and not created
- (22) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-32}{P_{32}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-34}{P_{34}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-35}{P_{35}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-36}{P_{36}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-42}{P_{42}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-43}{P_{43}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\) — *would give:* The Word who became flesh in Jesus is God, of God's nature and not created
- (23) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-37}{P_{37}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-44}{P_{44}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-55}{P_{55}}\\) — *would give:* The Holy Spirit is God
- (24) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-39}{P_{39}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-40}{P_{40}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-51}{P_{51}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-52}{P_{52}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-53}{P_{53}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-56}{P_{56}}\\)
- (25) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-60}{P_{60}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-65}{P_{65}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-63}{P_{63}}\\) — *would deny:* The two witnesses of John 8:17–18 are two persons, the Son and the Father
- (26) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-61}{P_{61}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-66}{P_{66}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-64}{P_{64}}\\) — *would deny:* The Son asking on earth and the Father answering from heaven are two persons
- (27) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-71}{P_{71}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-59}{P_{59}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-76}{P_{76}}\\) — *would deny:* The Son is a person other than the Father, not the Father himself
- \\(\vdash\\) \\(\lnot \href{claims.html#claim-56}{P_{56}}\\) — *at issue, the denial of:* The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three persons

</div>

Grounded in scripture alone: Deuteronomy 6:4; 1 Corinthians 8:4 — "the LORD is one"; "no God but one", John 1:1 — "and the Word was God": God (θεός), without "the", John 1:3 — "all things were made through him", John 20:28 — "Thomas answered him, 'My Lord and my God!'", Acts 5:3–4 — "lie to the Holy Spirit … not to man but to God", John 1:1 — "the Word was with God", John 17:5 — "the glory that I had with you before the world existed", Matthew 28:19 — "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit", John 8:17–18 — "the testimony of two people is true … and the Father", Matthew 17:5; John 12:28 — the Father answers the Son from heaven, 1 Corinthians 8:6 — "for us there is one God, the Father".

### Readings, written down

<a id="nicenSupplementedReading"></a>
**`nicenSupplementedReading`**

**The supplemented Nicene reading**: every text and every Nicene reading,
"is God" as one essence; none of the rivals' readings.

```lean
def nicenSupplementedReading : Valuation Claim :=
  fun a =>
    match a with
    | Claim.wordIsAGod => False
    | Claim.firstbornIsFirstCreated => False
    | Claim.spiritIsGodsForce => False
    | Claim.sonIsACreature => False
    | Claim.wordIsGodsThought => False
    | Claim.gloryInGodsPlan => False
    | Claim.oneNameIsJesus => False
    | Claim.twoWitnessesAreSpiritAndMan => False
    | Claim.voiceIsAManifestation => False
    | Claim.othersRightlyCalledGods => False
    | Claim.isGodAsIdentity => False
    | x => True
```

<a id="witnessesAnsweringReading"></a>
**`witnessesAnsweringReading`**

**The Witnesses' reading, answering**: their readings, the others Scripture
calls "gods" rightly so called, and "is God" as identity.

```lean
def witnessesAnsweringReading : Valuation Claim
```

<a id="onenessAnsweringReading"></a>
**`onenessAnsweringReading`**

**The Oneness reading, answering**: its reading, Bernard's replies, and "is
God" as identity, so the Son not another than the Father.

```lean
def onenessAnsweringReading : Valuation Claim :=
  fun a =>
    match a with
    | Claim.wordIsAGod => False
    | Claim.firstbornIsFirstCreated => False
    | Claim.spiritIsGodsForce => False
    | Claim.sonIsACreature => False
    | Claim.wordIsAnotherWithGod => False
    | Claim.threeNamedInOneName => False
    | Claim.threePersons => False
    | Claim.triuneGod => False
    | Claim.twoWitnessesAreTwoPersons => False
    | Claim.voicesAreTwoPersons => False
    | Claim.isGodAsOneEssence => False
    | Claim.sonIsAnotherThanTheFather => False
    | Claim.othersRightlyCalledGods => False
    | x => True
```

### What the supplemented positions deliver

<a id="nicenCase_establishes"></a>
**`nicenCase_establishes`** ⚗

**The supplemented case still delivers LST's confession, and holds together.**
The confession follows from LST's three lines, as before. The lines added here,
from Tertullian, Athanasius, Basil and Metzger, conclude other things: that the
Son is another than the Father, not a creature and not "a god", and that "is
God" does not mean identity. They answer the rivals' readings; they do not carry
the confession.

What is novel: none of its arguments is new; Augustine, Harner, Tertullian,
Athanasius, Basil, Calvin, Sharp and Metzger made them. The library joins them
in one case.

```lean
theorem nicenCase_establishes : Establishes nicenCase
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="nicenCase_is_satisfiable"></a>
**`nicenCase_is_satisfiable`**

The supplemented Nicene case can be held without contradiction.

```lean
theorem nicenCase_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable nicenCase.premises
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="witnessesAnswering_establishes"></a>
**`witnessesAnswering_establishes`**

**The Witnesses, answering, still deliver their conclusion.**

```lean
theorem witnessesAnswering_establishes : Establishes witnessesAnswering
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="witnessesAnswering_is_satisfiable"></a>
**`witnessesAnswering_is_satisfiable`**

The Witnesses' position, answering, can be held without contradiction.

```lean
theorem witnessesAnswering_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable
    witnessesAnswering.premises
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="onenessAnswering_establishes"></a>
**`onenessAnswering_establishes`**

**The Oneness position, answering, still delivers its conclusion.**

```lean
theorem onenessAnswering_establishes : Establishes onenessAnswering
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="onenessAnswering_is_satisfiable"></a>
**`onenessAnswering_is_satisfiable`**

The Oneness position, answering, can be held without contradiction.

```lean
theorem onenessAnswering_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable
    onenessAnswering.premises
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

### Does "each is God, and they are two" hold together?

<a id="threeClaims"></a>
**`threeClaims`**

The three claims a reader may think cannot be held at once: the Father is God,
the Son is God, and the Son is another than the Father.

<div class="testimony-derivation">

- (1) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-59}{P_{59}}\\) — 1 Corinthians 8:6 — "for us there is one God, the Father"
- (2) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\) — The Word who became flesh in Jesus is God, of God's nature and not created
- (3) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-76}{P_{76}}\\) — The Son is a person other than the Father, not the Father himself

</div>

<a id="three_claims_hold_on_one_essence"></a>
**`three_claims_hold_on_one_essence`** ⚗

**The three claims contradict one another only with the identity step added.**
Written as three separate claims (the Father is God, the Son is God, the Son is
another than the Father), they can all be true at once, and they stay so with
Basil's reading added, which rules out reading "is God" as identity.

What this does not claim: that the one-essence reading is right, or that it does
more here than exclude the identity step. The check does not model what
"essence" and "person" mean; that analysis is not yet done.

What is novel: Basil's distinction is old; the check is the library's.

```lean
theorem three_claims_hold_on_one_essence : Satisfiable (threeClaims ++ [p
    Claim.isGodAsOneEssence, essenceExcludesIdentity])
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="three_claims_fail_on_identity"></a>
**`three_claims_fail_on_identity`** ⚗

**With Bernard's step from identity, they cannot all be held.** Read "is God"
as Bernard does, as naming the one God himself, take his step that two who are
each the one God are the same person, and grant that the Father and the Son are
both God: then the Son is not a second person beside the Father. So whoever takes
that step must give up one of the three claims, and Bernard gives up the third:
Jesus, as God, is "the Father manifested in flesh". The Witnesses take a step of
their own from the same reading, from "with God" to "not God", and give up the
second; that step is not part of this check.

What this does not claim: that the step is wrong, or that Bernard errs in
drawing what he draws from it. The step is rated `disputed`, because Aquinas
grants that each person is the one God himself and denies that they are
therefore one person (Aquinas, *Summa Theologiae*, part I, question 28, article
3, reply to the first objection).

What is novel: that both rivals reason from the identity reading is the
library's reading of their words; this check covers Bernard's step.

```lean
theorem three_claims_fail_on_identity : ¬Satisfiable (threeClaims ++ [p
    Claim.isGodAsIdentity, bothGodSoOne])
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

### What an opponent must reject

<a id="sonIsGodCase_is_satisfiable"></a>
**`sonIsGodCase_is_satisfiable`**

The case that the Son is God can be held without contradiction.

```lean
theorem sonIsGodCase_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable sonIsGodCase.premises
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="son_is_god_burden"></a>
**`son_is_god_burden`**

**The opponent's burden against "the Son is God".** The case runs by six
routes: John 1:1 and 1:3 read with Harner and Augustine, Thomas's words, Hebrews
1:8, Titus 2:13, Romans 9:5, and Philippians 2:10–11 read with Isaiah 45:23.
Every text is granted, so what an opponent can reject is a reading, and there is
exactly one way to overturn the case: reject all six. No smaller set does it, and
no other set does it.

It shows how much a reader must deny to hold that the Son is not God, given these
texts: the reading of every one of them. The Witnesses do deny each, with a
rendering of their own, cited at each step: "a god", "like 'a god'", "God is
your throne", "the great God and of our Savior", "God, who is over all, be
praised", and honour given "to the glory of God the Father". It does not show
that any of those renderings is wrong. Each route's reading is rated `disputed`,
and the weighing ranks a case by its weakest reading, so six routes weigh there
no more than one; the breadth raises the burden instead.

What is novel: each route is old. The proof that each carries the conclusion on
its own, so that an opponent must reject all of them, is the library's.

```lean
theorem son_is_god_burden : OpponentsBurden sonIsGodCase sonIsGodRoutes [] []
    [[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]]
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

**What an opponent must reject.** *The Son is God, by six texts* concludes that the Word who became flesh in Jesus is God. That conclusion is overturned exactly when every reading in one of these sets is rejected. Each set is minimal, and no other rejection overturns it:

1. *"The Word was God": of God's nature, and not made* (disputed); *"My Lord and my God!" (John 20:28; Augustine)* (disputed); *"Your throne, O God" (Hebrews 1:8; Calvin)* (disputed); *"Our great God and Savior" (Titus 2:13; Sharp)* (disputed); *"The Christ, who is God over all" (Romans 9:5; Calvin)* (disputed); *Every knee to Jesus, as to the LORD (Philippians 2:10–11; Calvin)* (disputed)

<a id="casePartyNode"></a>
**`casePartyNode`**

The package each party argues from.

```lean
def casePartyNode : CaseParty → ArgumentPackage Claim :=
  fun x =>
    match x with
    | CaseParty.lst => lstDeityCase
    | CaseParty.nicene => nicenCase
    | CaseParty.sonIsGod => sonIsGodCase
    | CaseParty.witnesses => witnessesAnswering
    | CaseParty.oneness => onenessAnswering
```

<a id="caseDispute"></a>
**`caseDispute`**

The weighing of the supplemented positions: every party can be held without
contradiction, delivers its conclusion, and has its steps rated.

```lean
def caseDispute : Dispute Claim CaseParty :=
  { node := casePartyNode, consistent := caseDispute._proof_1,
    sound := caseDispute._proof_2,
    rated := caseDispute._proof_8 }
```

<a id="caseDispute_defeats"></a>
**`caseDispute_defeats`**

**Who defeats whom**, all 25 pairs, each checked by Lean. The Witnesses
defeat each other party and are defeated by each. Oneness and the two
Trinitarian cases defeat each other over the persons. Neither Oneness nor the
six-route case defeats the other, because Oneness holds that the Son is God.

```lean
theorem caseDispute_defeats : ∀ (i j : CaseParty), caseDispute.defeats i j ↔
    (i, j) ∈ [(CaseParty.lst, CaseParty.witnesses), (CaseParty.witnesses,
    CaseParty.lst), (CaseParty.lst, CaseParty.oneness), (CaseParty.oneness,
    CaseParty.lst), (CaseParty.nicene, CaseParty.witnesses),
    (CaseParty.witnesses, CaseParty.nicene), (CaseParty.nicene,
    CaseParty.oneness), (CaseParty.oneness, CaseParty.nicene),
    (CaseParty.sonIsGod, CaseParty.witnesses), (CaseParty.witnesses,
    CaseParty.sonIsGod), (CaseParty.witnesses, CaseParty.oneness),
    (CaseParty.oneness, CaseParty.witnesses)]
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="caseDispute_supports"></a>
**`caseDispute_supports`**

**The six routes support the Oneness position**: their conclusion, that the
Son is God, is a starting point of Bernard's line from identity. Nothing else
supports anything. Because Oneness uses the Son's deity to argue that he is not
a second person, the drawing shows the six routes lending weight to Oneness's
attack on the two Trinitarian cases. That attack is reported, not counted, and
changes no verdict. Each pair is checked by Lean.

```lean
theorem caseDispute_supports : ∀ (i j : CaseParty), caseDispute.supports i j ↔
    (i, j) ∈ [(CaseParty.sonIsGod, CaseParty.oneness)]
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="caseDispute_partOf"></a>
**`caseDispute_partOf`**

**LST's case and the six routes are each part of the Nicene case.** Each
pair is checked by Lean.

```lean
theorem caseDispute_partOf : ∀ (i j : CaseParty), caseDispute.partOf i j ↔ i =
    j ∨ (i, j) ∈ [(CaseParty.lst, CaseParty.nicene), (CaseParty.sonIsGod,
    CaseParty.nicene)]
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

| 3 *The Son is God, by six texts* | 2 *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* | is part of |

The defeats are the cells of [`caseDispute_defeats`](#caseDispute_defeats), the supports the cells of [`caseDispute_supports`](#caseDispute_supports) and the parts the cells of [`caseDispute_partOf`](#caseDispute_partOf), each computed from the parties' premises and checked by the kernel. The attacks derived through support and through parts are reported, not counted: every verdict is computed from the defeats alone. 2 derived attacks are not defeats; the dispute leaves them open.

<a id="caseSettlesNothing"></a>
**`caseSettlesNothing`**

Every party is defeated by another.

**Nothing prevails outright: every party is defeated by another.**

- *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons (LST)*.
- *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*.
- *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *The Son is God, by six texts*.
- *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.
- *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 5 defeats and 0 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`caseDispute_defeats`](#caseDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. <a id="supplemented_forces_nothing"></a>
**`supplemented_forces_nothing`** ⚗

**Supplemented, the weighing still forces nothing.** Every party ties with
another, and every one rests on a reading rated `disputed`, so no rating breaks
a tie. Each reading aimed at a rival is answered by that rival with one of its
own, rated the same, and the Witnesses' renderings of the five added texts are
cited against each text's step. This is the result whichever side a reader
hoped for, and it does not say the readings are equally good.

What is novel: the weighing of these sources against the rivals' cited
replies.

```lean
theorem supplemented_forces_nothing : Framework.grounded caseDispute.defeats =
    ∅
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="nicenWithItsParts"></a>
**`nicenWithItsParts`**

The Nicene case, with LST's and the six routes, answers both rivals itself.

***One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* is accepted on some resolution.**

- A position holding *One God, three persons (LST)*, *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*, *The Son is God, by six texts* can be held.
- None of *One God, three persons (LST)*, *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*, *The Son is God, by six texts* defeats another, and each attack on them is answered from among them:
  - *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons (LST)*, and *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.
  - *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *One God, three persons (LST)*, and *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*.
  - *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*, and *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.
  - *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*, and *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*.
  - *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *The Son is God, by six texts*, and *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 7 defeats and 10 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`caseDispute_defeats`](#caseDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. <a id="nicene_case_defensible"></a>
**`nicene_case_defensible`** ⚗

**The supplemented Nicene case can be defended**, with LST's case and the six
routes: the three can be defended together against both rivals.

What is novel: the supplemented case is the library's assembly.

```lean
theorem nicene_case_defensible : Framework.CredulouslyAccepted
    caseDispute.defeats CaseParty.nicene
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="nicenAnsweredByOneness"></a>
**`nicenAnsweredByOneness`**

The Oneness position, with the six routes, can be defended, and leaves the
Nicene case out.

***One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* is not accepted on every resolution.**

- A position holding *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, *The Son is God, by six texts* can be held, and it holds *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*; *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* conflicts with *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*: *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*, and *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*.
- None of *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, *The Son is God, by six texts* defeats another, and each attack on them is answered from among them:
  - *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *One God, three persons (LST)*.
  - *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*.
  - *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.
  - *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *The Son is God, by six texts*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 7 defeats and 6 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`caseDispute_defeats`](#caseDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. Whether an attack survives turns on the attacker's weakest link and on the rating of what it attacks, so a changed rating can change the verdict. The weakest links:

- *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - In "the Word was God" (John 1:1) the Word has the nature of the one God — [Harner 1973](../../bibliography.md#harner-qualitative-anarthrous-1973); [Kibbey 2026](../../bibliography.md#kibbey-living-systematic-theology-2026), §3, The Triune God
  - By John 1:3 the Word is not among the things made — [Schaff](../../bibliography.md#schaff-nicene-post-nicene-fathers-1-7), §Tractates on John I.11
  - In Acts 5:3–4 Peter names the Holy Spirit God — [Calvin 1844](../../bibliography.md#calvin-commentary-acts-1844), p. 198
  - The Word of John 1:1 is God's thought and self-expression, not a second person — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 4 and 8, on John 1:1
  - The glory of John 17:5 was the Son's in God's plan before the world — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 8, The Preexistence of Jesus
  - The one "name" of Matthew 28:19 is Jesus; Father, Son and Spirit are titles — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 6, Matthew 28:19
  - The two witnesses are the divine Spirit and the man Jesus, of one person — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 8, Two Witnesses
  - The voice from heaven is a manifestation of the one Spirit, not a person — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 8, The Voice from Heaven
  - "Is God" says someone is the one God himself, the same one — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 8, Are Jesus and the Father One in Purpose Only?; [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 27
  - The Word who became flesh in Jesus is God, of God's nature and not created — [Kibbey 2026](../../bibliography.md#kibbey-living-systematic-theology-2026), §3, The Triune God; [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 4, Conclusion
  - an inference step — [Kibbey 2026](../../bibliography.md#kibbey-living-systematic-theology-2026), §3, The Triune God; [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 4, Conclusion; [Buzzard 2001](../../bibliography.md#buzzard-caveat-lector-2001), pp. 17–19
  - an inference step — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 8, Are Jesus and the Father One in Purpose Only?; [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 27; [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 28, a. 3
- *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*, weakest at *disputed*:

<a id="nicene_case_not_forced"></a>
**`nicene_case_not_forced`** ⚗

**The supplemented Nicene case is not forced.** The Oneness position and the
six routes to "the Son is God" can be defended together, and because Oneness
and the Nicene case defeat each other, no defensible group that holds Oneness
can hold the Nicene case.

What is novel: it weighs the library's assembly.

```lean
theorem nicene_case_not_forced : ¬Framework.SkepticallyAccepted
    caseDispute.defeats CaseParty.nicene
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="sonIsGodWithOneness"></a>
**`sonIsGodWithOneness`**

The six routes stand with the Oneness position as well as the Nicene.

***The Son is God, by six texts* is accepted on some resolution.**

- A position holding *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, *The Son is God, by six texts* can be held.
- None of *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, *The Son is God, by six texts* defeats another, and each attack on them is answered from among them:
  - *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *One God, three persons (LST)*.
  - *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*.
  - *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.
  - *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *The Son is God, by six texts*, and *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 7 defeats and 6 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`caseDispute_defeats`](#caseDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. <a id="son_is_god_defensible_with_oneness"></a>
**`son_is_god_defensible_with_oneness`** ⚗

**That the Son is God, by six routes, can be defended with Oneness too.** The
six routes can be defended together with the Oneness position, which also holds
that the Son is God. Among the parties, only the Witnesses' position defeats
them.

What is novel: the six routes are the library's assembly.

```lean
theorem son_is_god_defensible_with_oneness : Framework.CredulouslyAccepted
    caseDispute.defeats CaseParty.sonIsGod
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="sonIsGodAnsweredByTheWitnesses"></a>
**`sonIsGodAnsweredByTheWitnesses`**

The Witnesses' position, on its own, leaves the six routes out.

***The Son is God, by six texts* is not accepted on every resolution.**

- *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* can be held alone; *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* conflicts with *The Son is God, by six texts*: *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *The Son is God, by six texts*, and *The Son is God, by six texts* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*.
- *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* does not defeat itself, and answers each attack on it:
  - *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons (LST)*.
  - *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*.
  - *The Son is God, by six texts* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *The Son is God, by six texts*.
  - *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 8 defeats and 1 absence of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`caseDispute_defeats`](#caseDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. <a id="son_is_god_not_forced"></a>
**`son_is_god_not_forced`** ⚗

**That the Son is God is not forced.** The Witnesses' position, answering, can
be defended on its own, and it denies that the Son is God. Six routes do not
outweigh it, because each route's reading is rated `disputed`, as each of the
Witnesses' readings is, and the weighing ranks a position by its weakest
reading.

What is novel: it weighs the library's assembly.

```lean
theorem son_is_god_not_forced : ¬Framework.SkepticallyAccepted
    caseDispute.defeats CaseParty.sonIsGod
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="witnessesAnsweringAlone"></a>
**`witnessesAnsweringAlone`**

The Witnesses, answering, answer every attacker themselves.

***A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* is accepted on some resolution.**

- A position holding *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* can be held.
- *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* does not defeat itself, and answers each attack on it:
  - *One God, three persons (LST)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons (LST)*.
  - *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, three persons, supplemented (the Nicene case)*.
  - *The Son is God, by six texts* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *The Son is God, by six texts*.
  - *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)* defeats *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, and *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)* defeats *One God, one person, answering (Oneness)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 8 defeats and 1 absence of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`caseDispute_defeats`](#caseDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. Whether an attack survives turns on the attacker's weakest link and on the rating of what it attacks, so a changed rating can change the verdict. The weakest links:

- *A god, not God, answering (Jehovah's Witnesses)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - In "the Word was God" (John 1:1) God, without "the", means "a god" — [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 27; [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 2013](../../bibliography.md#new-world-translation-2013)
  - "Firstborn of all creation" means the first thing God created — [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 14
  - The holy spirit is God's active force, personified, not a person — [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), pp. 20–23
  - Scripture rightly calls others "gods", so the Word can be "a god" — [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 28; [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1986](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-questions-from-readers-1986), p. 31
  - "Is God" says someone is the one God himself, the same one — [Bernard 1983](../../bibliography.md#bernard-oneness-of-god-1983), §ch. 8, Are Jesus and the Father One in Purpose Only?; [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 27
  - "With God" (John 1:1; 17:5) is one person beside another, not a thought or plan — [Kibbey 2026](../../bibliography.md#kibbey-living-systematic-theology-2026), §3, The Triune God; [Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society 1989](../../bibliography.md#watchtower-should-you-believe-trinity-1989), p. 27
